note: CRuby's ary_join recurses over each element and inserts the separator between elements at every level, so an empty nested Array is an empty part and still contributes a boundary: `[[], 1].join("-")` is `"-1"`. The model flattened nested Arrays into leaves first, which dropped empty ones (`"1"`). The Lean fast path now renders each element as one part recursively (`joinValue`), and the prelude twin `__join_slow` does the same (`__join_one`/`__join_rendered`); the to_s-sensitive half of this file pins the twin. Verified against CRuby 4.0.5.
